note: Newly delivered, content-reviewed research and backfills; this is not a claim that every paper first appeared this week. Known first-online dates are retained; seven dates remain unverified. Source coverage is partial, including level 1/2 all-content and Science editorial-summary signature gaps. Full given author names remain unavailable for some entries. No private reader feedback was accessed. Figures remain at the original sources.

articles.title: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
articles.summary: DNA nanoswitch selection is coupled to sequencing to screen modulators of protein interactions. FIND is demonstrated with interaction-stabilizing nanobodies and small-molecule agonists. Its signal-selection strategy may inform biochemical transduction, although an implantable sensor is not demonstrated.
articles.editorSummarySignatureStatus: Unknown; official signature could not be verified in this run

articles.title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
articles.summary: Stamped NiTi sheets are stacked into porous structures designed to avoid buckling and splitting. The deposited abstract reports more than 100 million compression cycles and a specific cooling power of 3,850 W/kg. The structural fatigue strategy may transfer to cyclic mechanical devices; these results do not establish thin-film sensor lifetime.
articles.editorSummarySignatureStatus: Unknown; official signature could not be verified in this run

articles.title: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics
articles.summary: TomoSAXS maps fibril-to-fibre mechanics in intact intervertebral discs. Molecular pre-strain correlates with fibre-scale strain, revealing hierarchical load sharing and localized strain bridges. The method may help relate tissue architecture to mechanical sensing measurements.

articles.title: In vivo ultrasound–MRI 3D mapping of neuromuscular compartments reveals the neuromechanical architecture of finger-specific control
articles.summary: Dynamic ultrasound motion estimates are mapped into MRI volumes to reconstruct functional muscle compartments. In ten healthy participants, the recovered architecture agrees with classical anatomy and predicts surface electromyography distributions. This may support placement and interpretation of neuromuscular sensors.

articles.title: Magnetic omniconversion: Source-independent molding of magnetostatic fields
articles.summary: Linear magnetic materials passively reshape source fields into prescribed distributions within a finite source-free region. Analytical and numerical examples are accompanied by a proof-of-concept experiment. Possible uses include magnetic readout design and shielding, subject to the framework's geometry and material assumptions.

articles.title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
articles.summary: A multilayer electrode architecture on a three-channel liquid-metal fibre monitors sodium and potassium directly in blood. Rabbit experiments and human blood samples are compared with conventional measurements. The work is relevant to perioperative chemical monitoring; wireless operation and motion tolerance are not established by the abstract.

articles.title: A soft wireless bioelectronic patch for noninvasive modulation of cavernosal microenvironment in diabetic erectile dysfunction
articles.summary: A soft wireless patch combines microelectrodes, drug reservoirs and nanopores for localized transdermal delivery. The study reports improved perfusion, vascular repair and functional recovery in preclinical experiments. Its integrated delivery architecture may inform wearable therapeutic systems; clinical effectiveness is not established.

articles.title: Spatially Decoupled Donor and Acceptor Gradient Brush Particle Blends for Mechanically Robust, Fatigue-Resistant, and Recyclable Elastomers
articles.summary: Complementary hydrogen-bonding brush particles form reversible interparticle cross-links. The abstract reports tensile strength up to 18 MPa together with crack resistance, reprocessing and thermally assisted recovery. This offers a materials strategy for durable soft-device supports, rather than a demonstrated sensor endurance specification.

articles.title: Ion Accessibility Governs Electrochemically Effective Actuation in Carbon Nanotube Muscles
articles.summary: Changing the solvent while retaining the CNT architecture and ionic species strongly changes contraction. At 2.5 V the abstract reports 50.4% contraction in propylene carbonate and 2.1% in trimethyl phosphate. Spatial ion accessibility helps explain mechanically effective charge, offering a useful electrochemical-to-mechanical design principle.

articles.title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
articles.summary: A waveguiding liquid-crystal elastomer core and conductive sheath combine photothermal actuation with resistive self-sensing. The abstract reports contractions up to 38% and independent optical addressing of fibre arrays. This may guide integrated actuation and sensing in confined spaces.

articles.title: Structure‐Encoded Magnetic Anisotropy in Super‐Tough Magnetoelastic Aramid–Silk–Magnetite Fibers
articles.summary: Aligned aramid–silk–magnetite fibres encode magnetic anisotropy through hierarchical structure and dipolar interactions. Mechanical strain reconfigures magnetic response and enables torque actuation; the abstract reports toughness up to 820 MJ/m³. This is directly relevant to magnetomechanical composite design, without establishing bioresorption or implant safety.

articles.title: A Liquid Metal Route for Designing Stretchability and Nanoporosity in Gold Thin Film Bioelectrodes
articles.summary: A room-temperature liquid-metal route forms nanoporous gold on stretchable PDMS, with carbon nanofibres supporting conduction across cracks. The abstract reports conduction at 80% strain and an 11% relative resistance change after 2,000 cycles at 20% strain. These are useful reliability benchmarks for thin-film bioelectrodes, not evidence of drift-free sensing.

articles.title: Intrinsic‐Decoupled Biomimetic Two‐Dimensional Sensing Enabled by Positive‐Negative Dielectric Heterostructures for Pressure Visualization
articles.summary: A graded-modulus dielectric heterostructure and differential capacitance reduce overlap between normal and tangential deformation fields. The abstract reports monotonic responses over 0–30 N and 1.5° angular resolution at 20–30 N. Its force-separation mechanism is relevant to tactile arrays, with performance limited to the calibrated conditions.

articles.title: Hydrogel‐Based Method for High‐Resolution Measurements of Contact Mechanics in Rapid Biological Adhesives: A Case Study in Cuttlefish Tentacle Strikes
articles.summary: A gelatin-based hydrogel retains transient sucker imprints for high-speed video and OCT analysis. Calibration against controlled indentations links imprint geometry to contact force. This provides a transferable method for rapid, spatially distributed biological contact measurements.

articles.title: Architected Bio‐Based Iontronic Skin With Dual‐Mode Pressure and Strain Sensing
articles.summary: A printed ionogel with more than 80% bio-based carbon supports separate capacitive pressure and resistive strain channels. Gyroid architecture increases low-pressure sensitivity eightfold and accelerates strain response 4.6-fold in the reported comparisons. The work separates chemistry and geometry as design variables for e-skins; bio-based composition does not establish biodegradability.

articles.title: Interface-engineered liquid metal-composited hydrogels with high toughness and extreme flaw insensitivity for damage-tolerant wearables
articles.summary: Tannic-acid-coated liquid-metal droplets couple dynamically to a hydrogel matrix and blunt crack tips. The paper reports fracture energy of 12.43 kJ/m² and sensing after mechanical damage. This supports damage-tolerant soft interfaces; it is an older, newly discovered backfill first available online on 26 August 2026.

articles.title: Triboelectric E-Fibers: Toward energy-autonomous wearable electronics
articles.summary: This review connects triboelectric fibre structure and manufacturing with energy harvesting, sensing and electronic textiles. It discusses integration and evaluation challenges rather than establishing one new device benchmark. Published online on 25 August 2026, it is included as a newly discovered backfill; peak power is not continuous delivered power.

articles.title: Fracture-mediated percolation governs electrical activation in liquid metal composite conductors
articles.summary: Imaging and electromechanical measurements identify matrix cracking as a pathway to conductive percolation in liquid-metal composites. A fracture-based framework links activation across droplet sizes and composite architectures. The result informs mechanically activated soft interconnects; it was published online on 29 October 2026 and is newly delivered as backfill.

articles.title: Low-voltage, ultra-broadband wearable MEMS ultrasound: a frequency-merged, wafer-scale framework for continuous in vivo cardiovascular imaging and monitoring
articles.summary: A frequency-merging pMUT architecture combines low-voltage drive with broad acoustic bandwidth. The abstract reports 81.7% bandwidth at 5 Vp, 9 cm phantom penetration and monitoring for up to nine hours under limited daily postural activity. The reported 2.2 mmHg blood-pressure deviation is promising for continuous hemodynamics; phantom depth and strenuous-motion tolerance must be assessed separately.

articles.title: Machine-knitted magnetoactive textiles for wireless charging, biomechanical sensing, and haptic feedback
articles.summary: Magnetic fibres and machine-knitted electromagnets combine charging, motion sensing and haptic output in one textile architecture. The abstract reports charging a 7.4 V battery, sensing motions up to 3,000 Hz and haptic forces up to 4.2 mN. This is directly relevant to bidirectional magnetomechanical wearables; the frequency statement does not establish the complete wireless acquisition rate.
articles.readingBasis: Official article abstract or indexed synopsis

articles.title: Skin-mimetic adaptive gradient electrode for ambulatory noninvasive brain-computer interfaces
articles.summary: A gradient hydrogel electrode combines a compliant scalp interface with a firmer circuit connection and sustained electrolyte release. The abstract reports EEG recording for more than eight hours during movement and fourteen hours at rest, with typing accuracy above 94%. The design informs mechanical matching and motion-artifact management in ambulatory interfaces.
articles.readingBasis: Official article abstract or indexed synopsis

articles.title: Liquid metal interfaces for component mounting on kirigami stretchable substrates
articles.summary: Liquid-metal mounting interfaces reduce the mechanical constraint imposed by rigid components on kirigami substrates. The abstract reports maintained resistor-array connectivity up to a device strain of 2.0. This offers a packaging strategy for integrating conventional components with highly deformable electronics.

articles.title: Adaptive tunable sensing system inspired by scorpions for dynamic vibration perception in unstructured environments
articles.summary: A scorpion-inspired system switches among three sensing configurations in response to incoming vibration signals. Its tunable response addresses a broad amplitude range and supports robot gait adaptation. The concept may inform adaptive sensor front ends; reported gauge factors depend on the selected configuration and strain range.

articles.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy
articles.summary: Orally delivered nickel-ferrite/barium-titanate particles adhere to the stomach lining through capsaicin targeting. Magnetic stimulation generates electrical pulses that engage vagal pathways through the gut–brain axis. Animal-model findings motivate non-invasive magnetoelectric interfaces, without establishing clinical efficacy.
articles.readingBasis: Official article abstract or indexed synopsis

articles.title: Millisecond olfaction system with in-sensor feature extraction
articles.summary: The official article listing describes extraction of early adsorption kinetics for rapid artificial olfaction. This links front-end sensing with feature computation for fast gas quantification. It may inform event-driven sensor processing; this review is limited to the official indexed synopsis, not the full performance dataset.
articles.readingBasis: Official article abstract or indexed synopsis

articles.title: A smart nose for robots through in-sensor computing
articles.summary: This News & Views discusses rapid robotic olfaction using an analogue front end that extracts early adsorption information. It is commentary on the companion research, not an independent device experiment. The relevance is the connection between sensing latency and autonomous action.
articles.readingBasis: Official article abstract or indexed synopsis

articles.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
articles.summary: AutoDNA coordinates more than twenty instrument types across over 11,000 steps for biomolecular operations. The abstract reports a 3.2-fold improvement in concurrent protocol execution and demonstrations spanning synthesis, sequencing and DNA storage. It provides an adjacent model for laboratory workflow design, not evidence that all experimental reasoning can be automated.
articles.readingBasis: Official article abstract or indexed synopsis

articles.title: Large-stroke thin haptic interface for restoring pressure and friction in virtual reality
articles.summary: A skeleton-network haptic interface provides a 12 mm stroke from a 0.8 mm-thick contact structure. Buckling beams and conical springs support continuous normal and tangential stimulation, with human perception tests. This older article, first online on 12 October 2026, offers a thin-display design strategy; stroke-to-thickness ratio is not material strain.

articles.title: Implantable neural chip with electrochemical sensing and optogenetic stimulation for monitoring of cholinergic pharmacological responses
articles.summary: An implantable neural chip combines acetylcholine electrochemical sensing, optogenetic stimulation and miniature wireless measurement. The institutional account describes monitoring cholinergic responses to pharmacological intervention. This newly delivered backfill was published on 14 October 2026; review used verified metadata and the institution's substantive account, not full text.
articles.readingBasis: Verified metadata and substantive institution account

articles.title: Smart contact lens for personalized glucose level sensing and forecasting
articles.summary: A smart contact lens combines tear-glucose sensing with personalized analysis and forecasting. Lyophilization and a hydrogel coating address enzyme stability and wearing comfort. Tear measurement must be distinguished from blood-glucose inference; the first-online date remains unverified and is not inferred from the issue month.

articles.title: From actuation to autonomy: Physical and artificial intelligence in magnetic robots
articles.summary: This Perspective examines the combination of physically encoded responses and computational control in magnetic robots. It connects material structure, robot morphology and collective interactions with autonomy. It may guide actuation–sensing integration, but does not provide a new device benchmark; the first-online date remains unverified.

articles.title: Magnetoactive Hydrogels to Probe Curvature‐Directed Endothelial Cell Mechanosensing
articles.summary: A magnetoactive hydrogel changes endothelial-monolayer curvature on demand. The study links curvature to YAP localization and junctional changes while isolating geometry from shear-stress inputs. It offers a useful controlled platform for vascular mechanobiology, rather than an in vivo flow monitor.

articles.title: Hypoxia‐Guided Magnetic Catheter for Localization and Minimally Invasive Intervention in Early‐Stage Lung Cancer
articles.summary: A magnetic catheter integrates navigation, hypoxia-sensitive fluorescence and intervention channels. Tests include bronchial phantoms and porcine lungs, with bending characterized under a 40 mT field. The system is relevant to integrated catheter sensing and actuation; simulated lesions do not establish clinical cancer detection.

articles.title: Bioprinted Stiffness‑Tunable Pancreatic Microniches to Decode Early Tumor Initiation Mechanisms
articles.summary: Microvalve printing creates stiffness-tunable pancreatic microniches for primary mouse acini. Fourteen-day studies examine how matrix mechanics interact with oncogenic Kras during early reprogramming. This offers an adjacent model for controlled tissue-mechanics experiments, without establishing a human diagnostic stiffness threshold.

articles.title: A microcantilever-based current sensor with magnetic transduction for AC/DC measurement
articles.summary: A magnet-integrated piezoresistive cantilever converts conductor-field gradients into quasi-static bridge signals. Carrier excitation and lock-in detection reduce bridge-referred DC noise from 0.454 to 0.114 μV RMS in the reported comparison. This is a transferable magnetic–mechanical readout architecture; the 2.09 nN force resolution is a theoretical noise limit.

articles.title: Reconfigurable surface acoustic wave platform for particle concentration, sorting and in situ Raman identification on a single lithium niobate chip
articles.summary: A reconfigurable lithium-niobate chip uses traveling, standing and focused acoustic fields for particle handling and Raman identification. The abstract reports retention of irregular fragments for at least thirty seconds. The functions were characterized separately, so a fully integrated continuous workflow should not be inferred.

articles.title: A single-step injectable Janus-adhesive hydrogel for endoscopic gastrointestinal fistula repair
articles.summary: A thermoresponsive hydrogel forms a Janus-adhesive seal through a single-step injectable process. Rat and minipig experiments evaluate endoscopic gastrointestinal fistula repair. Its wet-tissue interface and deployment strategy offer adjacent lessons for minimally invasive devices.

articles.title: Re-timing mortality risk through individualized modelling of lifespan trajectories
articles.summary: A retinal-image biomarker maps mortality risk into individualized trajectories with external cohort validation. The work examines disease-related patterns and risk associations. It offers an adjacent example of longitudinal risk representation, without establishing precise individual lifespan prediction.

articles.title: Magnetoelectric Wireless Power Transfer Receivers for Sub-Millimeter Scale Implantable Bioelectronics
articles.summary: A MEMS magnetoelectric receiver combines piezoelectric and magnetostrictive thin films within a 770 × 360 × 2.25 μm footprint. The preprint reports 1 μW into 10 kΩ at a 100 kHz resonance under a 205 μT RMS field. It is directly relevant to powering small implants, but does not establish long-distance in vivo operation. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Magnetic Johnson noise from arbitrarily shaped conductors: experimental validation of the fluctuation-dissipation finite-element method
articles.summary: A SQUID gradiometer array tests finite-element predictions of magnetic Johnson noise from complex conductors. Calculations reproduce measured amplitudes and frequency dependence. The method may support sensor-array and shielding noise budgets. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Differentiable topology optimization for high-fidelity acoustic holography beyond the thin-element approximation
articles.summary: Differentiable topology optimization accounts for propagation through acoustically thick lenses. The preprint compares 45 configurations and reports hydrophone and ex vivo skull validation. It may inform transcranial field design and treatment of model mismatch. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
articles.summary: A constrained physics-informed network estimates the shear piezoelectric coefficient from sparse wavefield observations. Boundary and initial conditions are imposed through the output representation. Results use manufactured and finite-element data, not experimental coefficient measurements. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
articles.summary: A continuum model links coupling-tether geometry to mode splitting and dissipation dilution. Finite-element examples include a 17.7 Hz splitting for a specified geometry. The work may guide coupled resonator design; experimental validation is not reported in the abstract. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: The Agentic AI Kerr Lab: LLM Agents for Kerr Microscopy Experiments with Magnetic Skyrmions
articles.summary: An agent coordinates Kerr imaging, analysis and excitation using CNN-derived skyrmion observables. Hardware actions are checked independently against a deterministic policy. This offers an adjacent example of laboratory automation rather than biomedical sensing validation. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Analog signal processing, storage, and demultiplexing via in-materia wave-based computing
articles.summary: A reconfigurable elastic platform uses shape-memory-alloy transitions to manipulate mechanical waves. The framework addresses gating, delay, retention and frequency demultiplexing. It offers an exploratory route to mechanical front-end processing. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Surface chemistry as data for level-set simulation of etching and deposition
articles.summary: A data-driven surface-reaction representation supplies rate laws and velocities to the ViennaPS level-set simulator. One compiled model is applied to eight deposition and etching chemistries. The approach may support reusable MEMS process modelling. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Mesoscale Soft Robotics for Mechanically Perturbing and Functionally Monitoring Responses in Human Organoids
articles.summary: A mesoscale soft robotic interface delivers programmable forces while recording mechanical and electrophysiological responses. Experiments examine cortical-organoid trauma responses and rhythm changes in stretched cardiac rings. This is relevant to integrated force delivery and tissue sensing. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Measurement-Dependent Parameter Recoverability in Neural Cardiovascular LPN Inference
articles.summary: A probabilistic framework studies cardiovascular parameter recovery in 650,000 synthetic cases. Accurate reconstruction of observations does not guarantee recovery of generating parameters. This motivates identifiability and uncertainty analysis for hemodynamic decoding; the study is simulation-based. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Based Early Prediction of Neural Microelectrode Lifetime Under Accelerated Aging Conditions
articles.summary: Early electrochemical features predict impedance-defined microelectrode lifetime under accelerated aging. The reported device-level error is 13.90% MAPE, with additional calibration needed across fabrication batches. This is relevant to implant reliability datasets, without establishing in vivo lifetime. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Injectable Nanoparticles Assemble In Situ into Modular, Functionally Segmented Brain Electrodes
articles.summary: Injectable nanoparticles assemble into soft, functionally segmented electrodes in chicken embryo brains. Active and inactive sections spatially separate stimulation and electroporation functions. The work informs in situ neural interfaces, with evidence limited to the reported preclinical setting. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Raman-probe-derived biomarkers account for cartilage composition, structure, and viscoelastic properties
articles.summary: An arthroscopy-compatible Raman needle probe is compared with indentation and biphasic models in equine cartilage explants. Raman biomarkers account for 81% of variation in equilibrium modulus. The study offers a cross-modal composition–mechanics calibration strategy, rather than clinical modulus validation. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Cross-species structure-mechanics prediction in the intervertebral disc
articles.summary: Synchrotron imaging, fibre tracing and digital volume correlation link disc structure to mechanical vulnerability. Rat and minipig samples undergo compression, while human samples contribute structural comparisons, with three specimens per species. The framework may support structure-informed mechanical assessment. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Bioresorbable, Injectable In Situ-Formed Electroactive mRNA-Delivering Device for Precision Gene Therapy after Myocardial Infarction
articles.summary: An injected formulation forms a transient conductive mRNA-delivery electrode over the injured heart. Preclinical experiments report local electrotransfection and functional improvement after myocardial infarction. The concept is relevant to temporary, resorbable therapeutic interfaces. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Feasibility of an anterior abdominal electrode array for non-invasive measurement of uterine contractions across the menstrual cycle
articles.summary: An anterior abdominal electrode array is evaluated for monitoring uterine contractions across the menstrual cycle. Simulations and experiments address signal coherence without subject-specific anatomical scans. This is a feasibility step toward longitudinal wearable electrohysterography. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Stop-Flow Lithography Using Hydrodynamic Flow Resistance Regulation and Hydraulic Compliance Minimization for Size-Tunable Anisotropic Multilayered Microparticles Fabrication
articles.summary: A stop-flow lithography platform regulates hydraulic resistance and reduces inlet compliance. Modelling identifies stored fluid volume and PDMS deformation as key causes of stopping delay. The method may improve multilayer microparticle fabrication. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Differential sensing with imprinted and non-imprinted organic electrochemical transistors reduces calibration drift in wearable sweat cortisol sensors
articles.summary: Matched imprinted and non-imprinted OECT channels provide a differential cortisol signal. Four calibrations over 14 days in artificial sweat show lower drift, with exploratory sweat data from one participant. The reference-channel design is relevant to longitudinal sensing. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: An Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Organ-Specific CyclicMultiaxial Loading and Differentiation of Progenitor Cells
articles.summary: A microfluidic platform applies programmable multiaxial cyclic loading to tissue scaffolds. Computation and experiments characterize strain fields, with cardiac tissue as a proof of concept. The platform may support controlled mechanobiology experiments. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: Wearable Estimation of Knee Joint Contact Forces: SiMPLeSENSE, a Simulated-IMU Pipeline Validated Against In Vivo Loads
articles.summary: Simulated IMU signals drive musculoskeletal estimates compared with instrumented knee implant loads. The abstract reports median errors of about 0.3–0.5 body weights and sensitivity to orientation errors. The pipeline uses motion-capture-derived inputs, so deployment with real wearable IMUs remains a separate validation step. Not peer reviewed.

articles.title: In situ acoustic manufacturing of conformal brain–computer interfaces
articles.summary: Focused ultrasound triggers localized cross-linking to print conformal conductive electrodes in situ. The abstract reports about 200 μm resolution, 30-second gelation and three-month recording stability, with rodent and pig demonstrations. This is relevant to tissue-matched neural interfaces. Preprint, not peer reviewed; Nature Portfolio submission does not imply journal acceptance.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified

articles.title: PA-SfM: Tracker-free freehand 3D photoacoustic imaging via differentiable acoustic radiation
articles.summary: A differentiable acoustic model jointly estimates view transformations and reconstructs freehand 3D photoacoustic volumes. Simulations, animal experiments and human imaging assess the approach, with controlled comparisons reporting PSNR above 40 dB and SSIM around 0.98. The joint pose–signal inversion may inform motion compensation. Preprint, not peer reviewed; portfolio submission is not journal acceptance.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified

articles.title: Characterizing the Spatiotemporal Boundaries of Functional Ultrasound for Brain Decoding
articles.summary: Controlled whisker stimulation in awake head-fixed mice characterizes spatial and temporal information retained in functional-ultrasound blood-volume signals. The experiments examine stimulus identity, duration and paired-event separability. This provides useful constraints on interpreting hemodynamic decoding resolution. Preprint, not peer reviewed; it is not a free-behaviour monitoring demonstration.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified

articles.title: Multimodal imaging maps spinal glymphatic transport in health and its disruption after injury
articles.summary: MRI and tracer studies distinguish spinal fluid propagation from tissue clearance after injury. Faster intrathecal propagation coexists with impaired clearance and tracer retention for up to seven days in the reported model. The distinction may guide interpretation of CSF and edema monitoring. Preprint, not peer reviewed; pressure and viscosity are not directly measured.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified

articles.title: PINPOINT enables non-destructive nanoscopic quality control of individual lipid nanoparticles and their mRNA cargo
articles.summary: Super-resolution and single-particle fluorescence measurements jointly profile lipid nanoparticle morphology and mRNA cargo. The platform reveals heterogeneity obscured by ensemble measurements. This is an adjacent example of multiparameter quality control at the individual-unit level. Preprint, not peer reviewed; Nature Portfolio submission is not acceptance.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified

articles.title: M³Sculptor: A Knowledge-Driven Multimodal-Agent Framework for Automated Metamaterial Design
articles.summary: A multi-agent framework reconstructs metamaterial candidates from literature images and evaluates them through computational homogenization. Symmetry restoration and morphological operations improve target matching within five rounds from 34.13% to 83.25% under the stated tolerance. These are computational design results, not fabrication yields. Preprint, not peer reviewed; list-page posting date was observed on the verified portfolio filter.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified

articles.title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
articles.summary: HealthJev separates shared medical rules from private longitudinal memory and filters lessons before reuse. Evaluation includes ninety-day simulated interactions for twenty users derived from MIMIC-IV trajectories and additional benchmark tasks. This may inform longitudinal data systems, but is not a prospective health-management trial. Preprint, not peer reviewed; portfolio submission is not journal acceptance.
articles.readingBasis: Visible abstract and expanded author list; Nature Portfolio filter and status verified
